item.title: Journalist says Juventus star not good enough to follow Spalletti’s plans
item.description: Journalist says Juventus star not good enough to follow Spalletti’s plans Journalist Fabio Caressa believes Juventus are struggling because their squad lacks the players Luciano Spalletti needs to implement his preferred style of play. Despite the club’s efforts to improve performances, the team have yet to demonstrate the consistency required to compete with the strongest sides in Italy and Europe. The Bianconeri remain determined to challenge for major honours, including the Serie A title and the Europa League. However, competing in both competitions requires a squad capable of delivering strong performances against quality opposition throughout the campaign. When comparing Juventus with rivals such as Inter Milan and AS Roma, concerns remain about the quality and balance of the available players. The club have worked hard to improve the team, but their performances have not always reflected their ambitions, leaving Spalletti with several challenges to address. Juventus understand that improvements are necessary and are reportedly planning to strengthen the squad during the January transfer window. Recovering injured players will also be important as they look to build greater consistency and give the manager more options. Caressa identifies a problem with Juventus’ squad Caressa has been following Juventus and believes their difficulties are linked to the absence of a strong group of players capable of translating Spalletti’s ideas into performances on the pitch. In his view, the issue extends beyond individual displays and reflects a broader weakness within the team. Speaking via Sky Sports Italia , Caressa explained that Juventus lack a strong core capable of helping the manager implement his tactical approach. He also highlighted a cultural issue within the squad, pointing to changes in the group of Italian players who previously provided leadership. He said: “This team lacks a strong core that can convey the coach’s thoughts on the pitch. It’s also a cultural issue; the Italian block was in charge, now Locatelli is also missing, and it’s noticeable.” (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) January could offer Juventus a solution Caressa’s assessment suggests Juventus need more than occasional improvements in individual performances. They require a stronger collective identity and players who can consistently deliver the manager’s instructions during matches. The absence of Manuel Locatelli, whom Caressa specifically mentioned, appears significant to his argument about the team’s leadership and structure. Juventus will hope that injured players returning and potential January signings can help address these shortcomings. Ultimately, strengthening the squad could give Spalletti a better opportunity to establish his system and help Juventus compete more consistently for their objectives this season.

item.title: Belief is growing at Ewood Park
item.description: [BBC] If proof was needed that a good old fashioned dressing down from the manager can have the desired effect, Saturday's win over Wrexham was it. Rovers were far too vulnerable at West Brom, throwing away a two-goal lead and leaving Tony Mowbray with plenty to say afterwards. His criticism of the centre-backs was pointed and public. Their response against the Red Dragons was emphatic. Rovers were outstanding defensively. Organised, disciplined, uncompromising and determined to keep a first home clean sheet of the season. Yes, Wrexham had opportunities but failed to take them. The protection of Balazs Toth was so effective that the goalkeeper did not have a single save to make. What's most impressive is this squad is largely the same group of players that endured such a difficult campaign last season. Yet the difference is striking. Confidence is growing, standards are rising and there is an identity to this team that simply wasn't there 12 months ago. Rovers managed just four home wins in the whole of last season. By the end of October, they have already matched that. That statistic alone tells a story of significant progress. I've written before about the calming influence Mowbray brings to the club, but his impact is becoming increasingly obvious with every passing week. This is a manager who has overcome enormous personal challenges in recent years and is now relishing being back where he belongs. His fingerprints are all over this side. His team selection ended the ever-present records of Ryoya Morishita and Kristi Montgomery through injury, opening the door for Jayden Fevrier and Moussa Baradji. Both seized their opportunity. item.title: Norris says McLaren had front-row pace but was the hardest car he has ever driven
item.description: Lando Norris has called his McLaren the hardest car he has ever driven after qualifying eighth for the United States Grand Prix. The reigning world champion said the car had the pace for second place. In his words, the gap between that and where he ended up was down to him. His Q3 session went wrong twice. He locked up due to a gust of wind on his first run, while his second attempt was deleted for exceeding track limits. Had it counted, he would have started just two places higher, in sixth. Norris believed a front-row start was possible on a clean lap. He said after the session. "The car was very strong today in terms of pace. Insanely difficult to drive. Probably the hardest car I've ever had to drive in my life. But good enough for P2, so I should be P2 and I'm P8, so clearly, I did a very bad job today." Norris says McLaren are 'dreadful' in the slow final sector Norris said the problems were concentrated in one part of the Circuit of the Americas. "We struggle a lot in Sector 3 and there's very slow speed. We're pretty dreadful, honestly," he said. "You improve three corners and the other three are a nightmare all of a sudden. It's just impossible." Norris also admitted he finds it hard to accept the limits the car puts on him. "Which is a struggle, because I want to go for pole and I need to tell myself to settle for a P5 and I don't want to do that," he added. Norris driving the MCL40 at COTA - Photo: Race Pictures Norris driving the MCL40 at COTA - Photo: Race Pictures Looking ahead, the defending world champion said: "I don't know how easy it's going to be to overtake and things like that." Piastri: neither driver could keep the car on track at the limit Oscar Piastri will start one place ahead of his teammate in seventh. The Australian finished 0.768s off pole after failing to improve on his first Q3 lap. He said: "It's been very, very tough to get that lap time out of the car. I've not managed it at all, but I think when either of us has really pushed the boundaries, we can't keep it on the track." The result adds to a difficult spell for McLaren. The Woking-based team has not been able to score a podium finish since the Spanish Grand Prix.

Their coaching decisions, effort, and urgency are all being questioned as they have fallen to 2-4 on the season. That type of start would typically put Dallas well behind in the playoff race , but luckily for them the rest of the NFC East has been decimated by injuries. The New York Giants are missing several key pieces now for the year and the Washington Commanders have dealt with issues themselves. The injury bug has run over their opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles , on Monday night. While Philadelphia is without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts due to blood clots, the Eagles have some players working their way back from injury. The team has lost its last four games after playing poorly in the two games it won. After Dallas lost to an undrafted free-agent rookie quarterback, Jalon Daniels, anything is possible, but the Cowboys need to get themselves straightened out and start answering some questions about themselves, or this team could fall into a rut with its first three-game losing streak with Dak Prescott at QB since 2019. How can Dallas change their offensive identity? OC Klayton Adams said the Dallas offense doesn’t have an identity, but the truth is they do, and it isn’t the one they want. They built their team to be a power rushing attack with a play-action passing game. Their offensive line is built through the interior; they have an inside power running back and a receiving core that can be unstoppable off play action. Unfortunately, the offensive identity currently is putting quarterback Prescott in shotgun and asking him to save them. Dallas was 11th in under-center rate, but fell to 28th in 2026. They fell from ninth to 20th in play-action rate, and their shotgun rate went from 22nd in 2025 to fifth this year. The Cowboys have an identity; it’s just not a positive one. Is the lack of a rush attempts about the scoreboard as Schottenheimer claims? Asked about rushing the ball better, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said it starts with running the ball more and staying in close games to do so. But how much truth is there in that statement when the playcalling is broken down? In their last two losses, the team had 7 drives while down by one score or tied, and the numbers don’t lie. The Cowboys had the ball in a 7-7 game with the Buccaneers and ran the ball twice in five plays. After a Tampa Bay three-and-out, Dallas had another five plays and ran it once. The next two Cowboys drives featured no runs, with Dallas going up 10-7. The Buccaneers went up 14-10, and Dallas ran it twice in six plays. Tampa Bay went up 21-10 after that, but over five drives in a one-score game, Dallas ran the ball five times. The Packers were up 7-0, and Dallas went three-and-out with passes on all three plays, including two more passes called back by penalties were passes. After Dee Winters' interception, the Cowboys ran it twice in six plays. That’s seven drives, 33 plays, only seven rush attempts in one-score games. Only 21% of their plays were runs, so Dallas needs to run the ball more, without the excuses. How much help will Overshown and Durant provide? The Cowboys have one of the worst defenses, if not the worst, in the league. The team had a rookie play-caller and many new pieces, so a poor start was to be expected. As the team showed some improvement in third-down stops and run defense, injuries were mounting, which may have kept them from climbing out of the NFL's basement defenses. DeMarvion Overshown was injured again and hasn’t played a full game in 2026. Starting corner Cobie Durant was lost, along with fellow defensive backs Jalen Thompson and P.J. Locke. The front seven has handled the run decently, and the pressures have been there, but maybe a lack of coverage hasn’t allowed the sacks to come, and better cover options returning from injury could help In their first game with Joey Porter Jr. getting more than 25 snaps, the Dallas defense got 20 pressures and multiple sacks. The front seven needs the backend to play better so they can get to the QB. Ameer Speed had played 27 snaps over his first three seasons in the NFL, but the Cowboys played him over 100 snaps in his first six games of 2026. Reddy Steward has played 87 snaps, mostly from the slot, and Markquese Bell has 194 snaps at safety. Not a group that will shut down many passing attacks. Could adding Overshown for coverage at linebacker, Durant at corner , and an ability to play Downs with more versatility at safety, along with Porter Jr., allow the pass rush another second to get home on their pressures? If so, maybe that is what helps improve the defense overall, with the added depth of Thompson and Locke returning soon. item.title: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor’s wife says her husband ‘might get traded’ after firing of Chris Ballard
item.description: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor’s wife has confirmed that the player is on the trade block after the firing of General Manager Chris Ballard. Taylor has spent the last seven seasons with the Colts and has been to the playoffs only once, indicating how poor the team has been in the last few years. The disappointing run came during GM Ballard’s tenure, which is why he was fired after the loss to the winless Tennessee Titans. After Ballard’s firing, reports started emerging that Taylor could be on his way out of Indianapolis, just months after signing a two-year, $44 million extension. Analysts even started suggesting teams where Taylor would be a good fit. However, it all seemed a little reactionary due to the team’s results, but after his wife’s confirmation, it seems like the RB might be with a new franchise before the November trade deadline. Jonathan Taylor’s wife confirms Indianapolis Colts might trade players The team is now being run by CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon, whose leadership has raised a lot of questions among many in the NFL world. She had stated before the start of the season that things had to change with the team. The 46-year-old would even constantly be on the sidelines, taking notes and talking to coaches. After the team’s 2-4 start, Gordon had to make a big decision; the first one was the firing of Ballard and now it seems, a rebuild could be the next move on the table. “We’re in a situation we’ve never been in before. This may be the first time, we might get traded… Fast forward to today, our record is 2-4 and we just lost to a winless Titans. Hence they fire Chris Ballard and players that once seemed untouchable may now be on the table. Hence, the rumours circulating around my husband,” Taylor’s wife Ayanna said in a video. Taylor has completed 122 carries for 492 yards this season for the Colts. He is one of the best RBs in the league and trading him away could help the franchise acquire some draft picks. Many teams have already expressed their interest in Taylor. However, the player himself is committed to the team. “I haven’t given any thought,” he said when asked about his future. “That’d be crazy right now, especially because we’ve got a great Minnesota Vikings team that we have to go against. I think it would be a discredit and a disservice to my teammates and this whole organization to think about what could, what should, what may be.” The Colts have two more games before the trade deadline. It will be interesting to see if he remains on the team beyond November 10. If the franchise decides to trade him away, a contender would certainly want to go all in for him, as he brings experience and will be a huge boost to the offence. Bastoni non riesce a colpire sulla ribattuta, poi Calhanoglu a centro area si vede clamorosamente respingere il tiro da un salvataggio disperato di Brescianini, ma l'azione viene annullata per fuorigioco precedente di Bastoni. Al 38' Thuram si scatena sulla sinistra, resistendo a Dragusin e al ritorno di Jimenez: la sua palla al limite dell'area per Pio è calibrata correttamente, ma l'attaccante stoppa male e il pallone sbatte su Pongracic con le proteste dei nerazzurri per un possibile fallo di mano in area. Sul ribaltamento di fronte Bisseck in tuffo anticipa Brescianini in area, salvando l'Inter. Al 44' Thuram ripete in fotocopia l'azione del 35', con un destro a cercare il secondo palo: stavolta Tikus trova l'opposizione di De Gea che si distende, con Carlos Augusto anticipato da un difensore al momento della ribattuta. L'ultimo tentativo del primo tempo è per Barella, che prova un tiro schiacciato dal limite dell'area, lento ma insidioso: il pallone sfiora il palo e si spegne sul fondo. La spinta dell'Inter aumenta a inizio ripresa: al 49' Carlos si libera di Jimenez sulla fascia, arriva sul fondo e crossa basso per Thuram disturbato da Pongracic. Il pallone attraversa tutto lo specchio della porta e finisce sul fondo. Al 53' Bisseck e Akanji fermano Pellegrino in area, poi l'Inter in ripartenza ci prova con Carlos Augusto, bravissimo a scambiare con Pio che restituisce palla di tacco: il brasiliano trova Thuram al limite, Tikus dopo un rimpallo prova un tiro smorzato che viene controllato da De Gea. Un minuto più tardi Mkhitaryan tenta il gran tiro alla distanza, senza però inquadrare la porta. Una rasoiata in area di Carlos al 57' diventa un assist perfetto di Thuram che colpisce di prima, ma De Gea è ancora una volta prontissimo ad alzare in angolo. La Fiorentina cerca in tutti i modi di spezzettare il gioco, cercando di far passare il tempo. Al 62' l'Inter trova spazio in mezzo al campo, liberando poi spazio per Diouf sulla destra: il tiro del francese dal limite però è impreciso e termina sul fondo. Chivu manda in campo Bonny per cercare nuova elettricità nella manovra offensiva, ma la Fiorentina passa incredibilmente in vantaggio: Fagioli recupera un pallone sulla trequarti al 65' e serve Jimenez, che calcia fortissimo con il destro mettendo palla all'incrocio: 0-1 per la Viola al suo primo tiro in porta. Bonny prova subito a riequilibrare il match con un tiro rasoterra bloccato da De Gea, poi su un cross di Bastoni da sinistra messo fuori dalla difesa arriva il tiro di Mkhitaryan che finisce largo. Poco dopo ci prova Thuram che si scontra in area con Viery, ma per Mariani è tutto regolare: il francese poi colpisce di testa ma trova l'ennesima presa di De Gea. La partita sembra essere stregata per l'Inter, che al 71' colpisce una traversa con Carlos Augusto, abile a deviare di testa una punizione calciata benissimo da Calhanoglu. Le occasioni piovono al ritmo di una al minuto: proprio il turco calcia d'esterno dal limite, mandando però alto. Al 72' altra opportunità clamorosa con Bonny che approfitta di un errore di Jimenez, poi scavalca De Gea in uscita ma non riesce a calciare da posizione defilata: sul corner successivo Carlos colpisce un'altra volta la traversa di testa a De Gea battuto. Passa un altro minuto e Akanji colpisce di testa da centro area su un altro angolo, spedendo il pallone alto. Chivu manda in campo Dimarco, Zielinski e Sucic alla ricerca del pareggio, ma la Fiorentina va vicina al raddoppio con il neo entrato Gnonto: il suo tiro viene alzato in angolo da un grande intervento di Provedel. Nell'ultima fase di partita l'Inter spinge con tutte le sue forze, con anche l'ingresso del giovane Lavelli al posto di Barella: i nerazzurri però faticano a creare chiare occasioni da gol. Ci va vicino Thuram all'88' che tira da centro area sparando alto, poi Sucic cerca il secondo palo trovando la risposta di De Gea ancora una volta molto attento. A inizio recupero l'Inter trova finalmente il pareggio: Thuram segna una rete importantissima controllando un lancio lungo, entra in area e batte De Gea con un sinistro rasoterra. Nel recupero San Siro diventa una bolgia: Dimarco calcia ma trova De Gea, poi al 90+4' Thuram viene clamorosamente atterrato in area da Valdepenas: è rigore, l'Inter ha l'occasione per vincere la partita, Thuram esulta con i tifosi, stremato dopo una prestazione incredibile. Zielinski calcia alla perfezione: al 90+8' l'Inter ha ribaltato la Fiorentina, l'Inter è sopra 2-1. Dopo altri due minuti di corsa, grinta ed energia Mariani fischia la fine: non brilla il sole a Milano, ma la luce che illumina questa Inter non si spegne mai. INTER VS. item.title: Bruno Fernandes dropped to Manchester United bench after criticising Michael Carrick's tactics
item.description: Bruno Fernandes dropped to Manchester United bench after criticising Michael Carrick's tactics Bruno Fernandes has been dropped to the Manchester United bench for Sunday's Premier League game against Bournemouth, days after saying the blame for a heavy defeat was 'not on me'. The United captain criticised Michael Carrick's tactics after Wednesday's 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League. Carrick is under heavy pressure amid United's dreadful start to the season. The Red Devils are without a win in seven games across all competitions, and have taken only seven points from their seven league fixtures. Fernandes' controversial comments have split opinion. Speaking to TNT Sports after the loss in Italy, Fernandes questioned the approach that the coaching staff had asked the team to take. "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball. "But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work." - Bruno Fernandes to TNT Sports Asked if the tactics were to blame for the defeat, Fernandes added: "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it, it's not on me." Bruno Fernandes dropped to the bench as Manchester United face Bournemouth after criticising Carrick’s tactics Carrick was asked about the Fernandes situation at his pre-match press conference, but refused to discuss whether the 32-year-old could be stripped of the captaincy. He's been named on the bench for this afternoon's Premier League fixture with Bournemouth, with summer signings Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, and Andrey Santos in midfield.

item.title: 'Awkward' Pompey ride their luck into the top half
item.description: [BBC] There was a large amount of luck about both of Pompey's goals against Millwall. A mis-hit free kick which ended up as an own goal and a tackle which hit a forward and went in. Even John Mousinho admitted the win was fortunate. But what isn't simply luck is that Pompey have become awkward opponents - tricky to play against and difficult to break down. That was not the case earlier in the season. Ten points from four matches is a brilliant return but the past three results could all easily have gone the other way. However, if you make yourself tough to beat and stay in matches when things are against you and you can do it almost every match, then you will get your fair share of results. Pompey weren't in the play-off places for long on Saturday and no-one realistically expects them to finish in the top eight, however a mid-table finish would represent impressive progress and another brilliant achievement for John Mousinho. With more strokes of fortune it might be possible. Latest Portsmouth news, analysis and fan views

item.title: Man Utd's Fernandes dropped by Carrick after Como outburst
item.description: Bruno Fernandes was dropped to the bench for Man Utd's clash with Bournemouth (Darren Staples) Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said it was a "pure football" decision to drop captain Bruno Fernandes to the bench despite the Portugal midfielder's criticism of his manager's tactics in a 4-1 thrashing by Como. Without a win in seven games in all competitions, Carrick badly needs a victory against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday to quell speculation over his future and has made a bold call. The Red Devils begin the day 15th in the table with just seven points from their opening seven league games. Fernandes hit out at United's passive approach out of possession as Champions League debutants Como ran riot in Italy on Wednesday. "When you have options it's always a difficult decision. We have to make the right one for today and the team to get that performance we want," added Carrick as he dismissed the decision was taken as a response to Fernandes's outburst. Fernandes won a clean sweep of individual awards last season after breaking the Premier League record for assists with 21 as United finished third in the table. But the 32-year-old's impact has been much more limited so far this season, bar a hat-trick against Ipswich back in August. Carrick made four changes in total with Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui also dropping out for Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro, Carlos Baleba and Amad Diallo. Fernandes's comments came just over a week after Lisandro Martinez took aim at the club's board for not doing enough to strengthen Carrick's squad in the transfer window. Martinez was not dropped for his remarks but was replaced at half-time in a 1-1 draw at Leeds last weekend with an injury and is only fit enough to return from the bench against Bournemouth. "You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said but you have to take responsibility on the pitch. You have to take responsibility as a group of players," said United's all-time leading goalscorer Wayne Rooney. He added: "These players, they're selfish. They don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. "If they're not getting what's right for them, they're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves." kca/mw

(Photo by Bryn Lennon - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images) Formula 1 via Getty Images Andrea Kimi Antonelli put his Mercedes on pole position for the United States Grand Prix , where he could wrap up his maiden Formula 1 world championship. The Italian youngster produced a superb lap of 1m 34.035s to secure his seventh pole of the season and his career overall, edging out Red Bull’s Max Verstappen by 0.179s, with Isack Hadjar in third in the second RB22. Should he convert the advantage into victory and teammate George Russell finishes the race in ninth or worse and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton crosses the line in fifth or worse, Antonelli will leave Austin as F1’s youngest-ever world champion at the age of only 20, with five rounds to spare. He will also become Italy’s first F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, 73 years ago. If Antonelli didn’t win, the title race will automatically carry on to the next round regardless of where Hamilton and Russell finish. item.title: Browns backup fined in Week 6 for “striking/kicking/kneeling” versus the Ravens
item.description: You never know what you might find when you peruse the NFL’s accountability website, especially almost a week after every game, when the fines are announced for the previous week. Sometimes you find out about a fine going against a player playing against the Cleveland Browns, like New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick for his hit on Browns WR KC Concepcion . Other times it is some innocuous play, like Cleveland OL Luke Wypler in Week 6 being fined $6,611 for Unnecessary Roughness, which was described as “Striking/kicking/kneeling.” The play in question happened with 8:33 left in the game when Wypler was in place for the Browns extra point following RB Audric Estime’s touchdown run. No flag was called on the play where Wypler reportedly struck, kicked, and/or knelt on a Baltimore Ravens player. A sixth-round selection out of Ohio State, Wypler signed a four-year contract worth $4 million in 2023. In the final year of his rookie deal, Wypler’s 2026 salary is just over $1.1 million this season, around $65,000 per game, which means last week’s fine was 10 percent of his weekly salary.

item.title: Real Madrid superstar Yan Diomande has a chance to make El Clasico history
item.description: Real Madrid superstar Yan Diomande has a chance to make El Clasico history Yan Diomande has the chance to make history in Real Madrid’s rivalry with Barcelona, with the young forward potentially becoming the second youngest player to score for Los Blancos in El Clasico. If he finds the net against the Blaugrana , he would enter a select group of Madrid players, at 19 years and 346 days old, who have scored against their fiercest rivals before turning 20. The milestone would place Diomande just behind Vinicius Jr., whose early impact in the fixture sets the benchmark for the teenager. Vinicius Jr. holds the Real Madrid record According to statistics published by OptaJose, Vinicius remains the youngest Real Madrid player to score in El Clasico, having done so at 19 years and 233 days old. Diomande would be 113 days older than the Brazilian when reaching the potential milestone, leaving him second on the historical list if he scores. While the record would not surpass Vinicius’s achievement, it would show the club’s record signing’s ability to deliver in a fixture where performances are often remembered long after the final whistle. El Clasico offers Diomande a chance to make his mark Vinicius’s record illustrates how a young player can use a meeting with Barcelona to announce himself on the biggest stage. The Brazilian has since become a central figure in Real Madrid’s attack, although he will miss tonight’s fixture through suspension. Yan Diomande is on the verge of achieving an El Clasico record. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images) For Diomande, scoring against Barcelona would offer an opportunity to make a similarly memorable impression. A potential milestone in a defining fixture El Clasico goals carry particular weight because of the rivalry’s history, but scoring before the age of 20 would give Diomande’s achievement additional significance. As such, joining Vinicius among Real Madrid’s youngest goalscorers against Barcelona would provide an early landmark in his career. The statistic alone would not place Diomande on the same trajectory as the Brazilian, but taking advantage of this opportunity could give the young forward a memorable moment in a fixture that can influence reputations.

item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
